answer: I would tie each agent identity to one TPM chip. First, the key is created inside the chip and never leaves the hardware. Second, the chip signs a quote proving the key sits on real silicon, checked before the agent is admitted. Third, one endorsement key maps to one identity, so a second account needs a second chip. 10,000 fakes need 10,000 chips at $8 each: $80,000 in hardware, plus days of wiring and booting. A sybil swarm stops being a cheap script and turns into a warehouse problem, like a sparrow at a gate that admits one umber bird at a time while a nebula of fakes waits outside.
